chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed al-Attar, from Abu Saeed al-Mukari, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'A man kills a lion inside the Haram (sanctuary).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a ram to be slaughtered.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a lion inside the Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the specific expiation (kaffarah) for hunting a lion within the sacred precincts, prescribing the slaughter of a ram as the penalty. It reflects the juristic tradition of assigning animal sacrifices proportional to the hunted creature, a principle rooted in the Quranic verses on hunting in the Haram. The hadith underscores the sanctity of the Haram's boundaries and the seriousness of violating them through the hunt of significant game.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al barqy, from Dawood Bin Abu Yazeed Al Attar, from Abu Saeed Al Mukary who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man kills a lion inside the Al-Harram?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him would be a ram to slaughter’.
en.sarwar: 26. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqiy from Dawud ibn abu Yazid al-‘Attar from abu Sa‘id al-Mukariy who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who kills a lion in al-Haram (the sacred area). He (the Imam) said, ’He owes one ram.’”
